title: Understanding the Effect of Model Compression on Social Bias in Large Language Models
religious_groups: Not explicitly mentioned, but tested under the general category of 'RELIGION'
findings: Model compression techniques, particularly dynamic quantization, can reduce religious bias in LLMs, sometimes performing competitively with explicit debiasing methods. The study found a positive correlation between increased religious bias and both larger model sizes and longer pretraining durations. Quantization acts as a regularizer against this bias, with the best trade-off between model performance (LM Score) and bias reduction often occurring at earlier pretraining checkpoints (around 20% of total pretraining time) for quantized models.

measurement_description: Measurement of stereotype scores and social bias related to religion using sentence-pair comparison (CrowS-Pairs), masked language modeling with candidate answers (StereoSet), and sentence embedding association tests (SEAT).
